pattern: answered controls report the datum frame awaiting acceptance (issue #20)
evidence: Maintainer-approved issue #20 (https://github.com/pzfreo/specify-core-rust/issues/20) keeps unanswered defaults as suggestions, so an answered datum-dependent control is omitted until its frame is accepted. The approved review follow-up requires that omission to be visible: Rust adds awaits_datum_frame warnings naming the answered question, required frame and missing datum letters. Python implicitly accepts the frame and reports no pending control. tests/preview.rs, tests/turned_defaults.rs, tests/default_suggestions.rs and the WASM session regression cover position, partial ± locations, runout, flatness and datum controls, clearing the warning and writing semantic PMI after acceptance. Every departure and ordering change is exactly pinned by the documented UPDATE_RULE_DEFAULTS hook in rule_defaults_oracle.json.gz; frozen Python captures are unchanged.

pattern: unanswered defaults remain suggestions until explicitly accepted (issue #20)
evidence: Maintainer-approved decision in specify-core-rust issue #20 (https://github.com/pzfreo/specify-core-rust/issues/20): defaults stay suggestions until answered or explicitly accepted; only those are written as PMI, with no provisional drawing. Python preview fills unanswered defaults, but Rust preview/review and IntentEngine.writePmi now use only supplied answers and existing datums. Questions retain suggested values and reasons and unanswered ids remain open; an absent general_tolerance stays absent for draftwright general_tolerance_missing. Position/runout and datum-control answers wait for their datum frames; flatness on A waits for A. They cannot commit an unanswered datum suggestion. CLI/serve apply with explicit accept_defaults is unchanged, and #16 settling does not accept datum or general-tolerance suggestions. tests/default_suggestions.rs and crates/specify-core-wasm/tests/default_suggestions.rs verify GRM-02/GRM-03, partial answers, #16, explicit acceptance and semantic PMI readback; tests/preview.rs guards pending frames. Every complete Python/Rust departure remains pinned in rule_defaults_oracle.json.gz; original captures are unchanged.

Python preview fills unanswered defaults, but Rust preview/review and IntentEngine.writePmi now use only supplied answers and existing datums. Questions retain suggested values and reasons and unanswered ids remain open; an absent general_tolerance stays absent for draftwright general_tolerance_missing. Position/runout and datum-control answers wait for their datum frames; flatness on A waits for A. They cannot commit an unanswered datum suggestion. CLI/serve apply with explicit accept_defaults is unchanged, and #16 settling does not accept datum or general-tolerance suggestions. tests/default_suggestions.rs and crates/specify-core-wasm/tests/default_suggestions.rs verify GRM-02/GRM-03, partial answers, #16, explicit acceptance and semantic PMI readback; tests/preview.rs guards pending frames. Every complete Python/Rust departure remains pinned in rule_defaults_oracle.json.gz; original captures are unchanged.

pattern: a knurl's teeth derived from DIN 82, which Python's intent does not state
evidence: The maintainer's decision Q4/Q15 (docs/questions.md): AP242's turned_knurl needs at least three of number of teeth, tooth depth, root fillet, helix angle and hand beside the diameters and pitch (WR2; a diamond's helix angle, WR9), so the Rust rules derive them from the knurling standard and state each in the intent with its source, visible and editable ('standard': 'DIN 82', 'derived': key to source). Values: teeth round(pi x 10 / 1) = 31, the pitch kept at the tool's 1 mm; tooth depth P/2 = 0.5, the depth of DIN 82's 90 degree profile (IS 3403:1981 3.1; assumed, no table gives it); root fillet 0.1, the knurling wheel's crest radius up to 1 mm pitch (IS 6776:1980 4.3); a diamond's helix angle 30 degrees and no hand (DIN 82 type RGE). Checked in tests/threads.rs. Python's knurl states pattern, pitch and diameter only.

pattern: axis-first turned datum defaults and their dependent questions and intent
evidence: Axis-first turned datums: plain recognised principal cylinder with greatest total area (diameter breaks ties), excluding thread/knurl answers, recognition and PMI; interrupted shafts may use dominant bosses. Then a perpendicular contact/largest shoulder excluding recess walls unless the sole perpendicular face. Axial holes use diametral position to A alone; other holes keep the full frame. Runout uses A and is not offered on the datum diameter itself. A mostly prismatic body or different principal axes keeps plane datums. tests/turned_defaults.rs checks captured and live corpus geometry, overrides, offsets, cross holes and shoulder contacts. tests/fixtures/rule_defaults_oracle.json.gz is an additional exact regression guard on EVERY changed path and both values (including question ordering and all other rules); rules_oracle asserts that complete list before applying these verdict entries, so these scopes cannot hide further differences. pattern: measurement datums are proposed before dimensions, including in ± mode
evidence: Maintainer decision (draftwright-rust #122): choose measurement origins before dimensions. Rust proposes the same geometric A/B/C frame in ± mode and when no feature needs a geometric tolerance; turned parts retain their plain axis A and perpendicular shoulder B. Empty datum answers still remove them. ± hole locations use selected datum planes, never recomputed edge defaults; accepting ± defaults adds no position or geometric-control requirements. General baseline dimensions consequently use the proposed planes too. tests/tolerancing.rs, tests/locations.rs, tests/turned_defaults.rs and tests/writer.rs verify the default path, changed/removed origins, both modes and AP242 DATUM_FEATURE entities with no FCFs. The complete Python and Rust values, including both named no-datum scenarios, are pinned exactly in tests/fixtures/rule_defaults_oracle.json.gz before these verdict entries apply; original Python captures remain unchanged. Rules version 2 identifies this output change.

exact.prompt: What material is the part made from?
exact.why: Every drawing states the material; it also decides what tolerances are sensible.

exact.prompt: Which general tolerance applies to dimensions without their own?
exact.why: Covers every dimension without its own tolerance, so most features need no question.
exact.basis: ISO 2768-m (medium) is the usual general tolerance for machined parts.

exact.prompt: What surface finish applies where none is given?
exact.why: Ra 3.2 is ordinary machining; finer costs more. Faces that need better, such as bores and seals, can be given their own.
exact.basis: Ra 3.2 is what ordinary machining gives without extra passes.

exact.prompt: Is the part coated or treated?
exact.why: A coating changes the size of every face it covers, and the price.
Hardening is done after machining, and is written on the drawing.

suggestions.value: Solution treat and age to T6

exact.prompt: What should be done to sharp edges?
exact.why: Sharp edges cut hands and chip; a standard note says how far to break them.
exact.basis: Breaking edges to 0.2 is the common standard note.

exact.why: Position tolerances locate each hole from datums, for parts that must fit together. ± dimensions locate them on the drawing under the general tolerance, and need no datums unless a perpendicularity or parallelism is added.
exact.basis: Position tolerances, as holes usually take parts that must line up.

exact.prompt: What is the Ø62 hole for?
exact.why: A clearance, tapped or fitted hole each need different size and position tolerances.

choices.label: Nothing in particular
A pin, shaft or bearing fits in it
A pin, shaft or bearing fits in it
A pin, shaft or bearing fits in it
A pin, shaft or bearing fits in it

exact.prompt: What are the 6× Ø10 holes for?
exact.why: A clearance, tapped or fitted hole each need different size and position tolerances.

choices.label: Nothing in particular
A bolt passes through
A pin, shaft or bearing fits in it
A pin, shaft or bearing fits in it
A pin, shaft or bearing fits in it
A pin, shaft or bearing fits in it

exact.basis: ⌀10 is an ISO 273 clearance hole for M8.

exact.prompt: Position tolerance (Ø) for the 6× Ø10 holes, relative to A|B?

pattern: 0.5.5 / Optional fillet questions on captured inventory
evidence: Quiddity 0.5.5 #297 removes the fillet size floor. Specify offers the same optional radius question for every recognised fillet, including those in the frozen analysis. The none default adds no open question.

exact.prompt: What material is the part made from?
exact.why: Every drawing states the material; it also decides what tolerances are sensible.

exact.prompt: Which general tolerance applies to dimensions without their own?
exact.why: Covers every dimension without its own tolerance, so most features need no question.
exact.basis: ISO 2768-m (medium) is the usual general tolerance for machined parts.

exact.prompt: What material is the part made from?
exact.why: Every drawing states the material; it also decides what tolerances are sensible.

exact.prompt: Which general tolerance applies to dimensions without their own?
exact.why: Covers every dimension without its own tolerance, so most features need no question.
exact.basis: ISO 2768-m (medium) is the usual general tolerance for machined parts.

exact.prompt: What surface finish applies where none is given?
exact.why: Ra 3.2 is ordinary machining; finer costs more. Faces that need better, such as bores and seals, can be given their own.
exact.basis: Ra 3.2 is what ordinary machining gives without extra passes.

exact.prompt: Is the part coated or treated?
exact.why: A coating changes the size of every face it covers, and the price.
Hardening is done after machining, and is written on the drawing.

suggestions.value: Solution treat and age to T6

exact.prompt: What should be done to sharp edges?
exact.why: Sharp edges cut hands and chip; a standard note says how far to break them.
exact.basis: Breaking edges to 0.2 is the common standard note.

exact.prompt: What are the 4× Ø4.763 holes for?
exact.why: A clearance, tapped or fitted hole each need different size and position tolerances.

choices.label: Nothing in particular

A pin, shaft or bearing fits in it

exact.prompt: Position tolerance (Ø) for the 4× Ø4.763 holes, relative to A|B|C?

exact.basis: ⌀0.76 = H − F for a floating M4 bolt: this ⌀4.763 hole less the bolt.
